text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's monthly inflation in February quickened to 242.7 percent from 43.5 percent in January and cumulative inflation for the first two months was 391.9 percent, National Statistics Institute figures showed. @

-- Russia showed interest in the privatisation of big Bulgarian firms, such as Neftochim oil refinery and Balkankar forklift truck producer, Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency executive director Vesselin Blagoev said.
-- Russia is ready to invest some $600 million in seting up gas pipelines for transiting Russian gas through Bulgaria's territory, visiting Russia's deputy prime minister Oleg Lobov said. @
-- Bulgaria's Transport ministry plans to offer for sale still unprivatised equity in Bulgaria's biggest road transport carrier SO MAT, Transport minister Wilhelm Kraus said.
Germany's Willi Betz Internationale Spedition now owns 55 percent of SO MAT, employees hold 3.5 percent and 1.5 percent of the shares have been set aside to meet restitution claims.

-- Bulgaria is expected to apply for $150 million from the International Monetary Fund to stabilise local commercial banks before privatisation, Bulgaria's president's economic adviser Krassimir Angarski said.
-- Greek companies are expected to invest some $110 million in Bulgaria this year, Greece's trade representative in Bulgaria Georgios Dudumis said.

-- Bulgaria is expected to apply for $30 million from the World Bank to guarantee pensions and social payments when a currency board system is introduced in the country, Nikolai Nikolov, head of the National Insurance Institute said.

-- Bulgaria needs a more flexible system than a long-term implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime proposed by the IMF, visiting U.S. director of the Harvard Institute for Development Jeffrey Sashs said. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
